newsitem.title: UK: Ruhrgas urges caution in increasing gas use.
newsitem.headline: Ruhrgas urges caution in increasing gas use.

text.p: The vice-chairman of the German gas distributor Ruhrgas on Thursday warned against drastic restructuring of the European gas industry at a time when the market is working well.

Speaking at the gas executives summit conference Burckhard Bergmann said "the intensity of the debate on the restructuring of the European gas industry virtually creates the impression that it needs to be repaired immediately.

"Yet it is clearly not defective. If a product can register such a successful market development in Europe over the last 35 years as gas has and if the outlook for the next decade is even more favourable, then the industry has done a good job.
"What is disturbing is that only those who advocate radical change are considered progressive," Bergmann said.
He added that doubts remain over the wisdom of using gas for electricity generation in Germany.
"This deprives coal and in some countries nuclear energy of their very basis, of the only sector in which they can be used efficiently and in an environmentally acceptable manner," he said.

He pointed out the irony that 20 years ago policy makers demanded dispensing with gas-fired power stations, in the interests of security of supply, and that later it was argued that gas was too valuable to burn for electricity production.
"Now, experts are outdoing each other in their forecasts for the growth of gas, especially for use in power generation."
Bergmann also warned of the danger that liberalising markets may lead to more regulation not less.
"The risk of creeping regulation is wholly underrated," he said, adding that Germany's regulatory framework is already "very liberal" by international standards.
